बॉलीवुड एक्टर अजय देवगन विमल इलायची के विज्ञापन विवाद को लेकर एक बार फिर बड़ी कानूनी मुश्किल में फंसते दिख रहे हैं! 🚨

मामला यह है कि अजय देवगन ने महाराष्ट्र FDA के शो-कॉज नोटिस को चुनौती देते हुए बॉम्बे High Court में याचिका दायर की है। वहीं दूसरी तरफ, FDA कमिश्नर तुकाराम मुंडे ने ANI से बातचीत में साफ कर दिया कि एक्टर के कोर्ट जाने के बावजूद विभाग की कानूनी प्रक्रिया जारी रहेगी। ⚖️

याचिका में अजय देवगन का दावा है कि FDA का यह एक्शन मनमाना है और किसी भी उल्लंघन की कानूनी जिम्मेदारी ब्रांड एंबेसडर की जगह उत्पाद बनाने वाली कंपनी पर होनी चाहिए। उन्होंने यह भी कहा कि इलायची प्रोडक्ट से उनका कॉन्ट्रैक्ट अब खत्म हो चुका है।

दूसरी ओर, FDA का आरोप है कि विमल इलायची के जरिए असल में प्रतिबंधित विमल पान मसाला और गुटखा का सरोगेट प्रमोशन किया जा रहा है। इसी मामले में अजय देवगन, Shah Rukh Khan और Tiger Shroff को FSS Act की धारा 24 और 53 के तहत नोटिस जारी किए गए थे।

अब Chief Justice Mahesh C. Tripathi और Justice Advait Sethna की बेंच इस मामले पर 4 November को सुनवाई करेगी। 🔍

क्या विज्ञापनों के लिए स्टार्स को जिम्मेदार ठहराना सही है या सिर्फ कंपनी को? अपनी राय कमेंट्स में जरूर बताएं! 👇

ctx.text:
The actor had approached the Bombay High Court against the show-cause notice, while the food safety authority maintains that its adjudication process is underway.
The legal proceedings involving Bollywood actor Ajay Devgn over his endorsement of Vimal Elaichi are set to continue, with the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) maintaining that its adjudication process will move forward despite the actor approaching the Bombay High Court. The development comes amid increased regulatory scrutiny of celebrity endorsements linked to products that authorities allege are being promoted through surrogate branding.
Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe reiterated the department’s position while speaking to ANI. Addressing Devgn’s petition before the High Court, Mundhe said, “Even if the concerned person has moved the High Court, we have already started adjudicating proceedings and will proceed in accordance with the law.”
According to the FDA, an investigation conducted by the Assistant Commissioner has been completed, with the authority concluding that statutory violations had occurred. The matter has now been referred to the Joint Commissioner for formal adjudication. The proceedings are expected to continue unless the court issues an order restraining the department from taking further action.
The controversy follows show-cause notices issued by the Maharashtra FDA to Ajay Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff over their appearances in promotional campaigns for Vimal Elaichi. The regulator has raised concerns that advertisements for flavoured cardamom under the same brand identity could function as surrogate promotion for Vimal Pan Masala and gutkha. The manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of such products are prohibited under the relevant state food safety regulations.
The notices were issued under Sections 24 and 53 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, which deal with misleading advertisements and the penalties associated with them.
In his petition before the Bombay High Court, Devgn has challenged the notice, describing the FDA’s action as arbitrary. His plea reportedly argues that any enforcement liability should rest with the manufacturing company rather than the brand ambassadors. It also states that his contractual association was limited to cardamom products and that his involvement in the promotional campaign has since ended.
The matter is scheduled to be heard on November 4 by a division bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh C. Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna. The court’s hearing will take place as the FDA continues with its adjudication process, keeping the focus on the legal questions surrounding celebrity endorsements and alleged surrogate advertising.
